reimbursement_policies.policy_title: Diagnosis Code Requirement Policy, Professional and Facility - Reimbursement Policy - UnitedHealthcare Commercial and Individual Exchange
reimbursement_policies.evidence: This DRG description is not specifically addressed. The policy applies a general inpatient diagnosis-coding edit: reimbursement for inpatient UB-04 claims depends on submitting an acceptable principal diagnosis in Box 67 and following ICD-10-CM sequencing rules. If the principal diagnosis is inappropriate or falls into the invalid-principal-diagnosis grouping used for MS-DRG assignment, the entire inpatient claim may be denied.

The health plan reviews inpatient sepsis-related DRGs on a pre- or post-pay basis and may deny or adjust claims when the sepsis diagnosis is not clinically supported. The policy is limited to inpatient claims for members/enrollees age 18 or older and does not address sepsis screening or trauma DRGs.

provider_role_restrictions: physician or licensed independent practitioner documentation

reimbursement_policies.evidence: For California inpatient DRG-paid facilities, this policy is not DRG-title specific but can affect this trauma admission when it is an unplanned readmission. Separate reimbursement is not allowed for a same or related readmission that meets the readmission criteria; same-day related returns are treated as continuation of the original stay. Trauma-specific exclusions appear in some non-California state programs.

reimbursement_policies.evidence: Off-topic for this DRG pattern. The policy is a general inpatient readmissions policy and does not contain DRG-specific rules for these catastrophic admission groups. It only affects payment when the admission is an unplanned readmission within the policy window.
